rationale: C09 plausibly supplied a material drafting template for the child’s manpower policy. Its dedicated labor-supply provisions establish the same core administrative program: assessing defense and civilian labor requirements, coordinating labor supply with production and materials decisions, identifying critical occupations, developing induction and deferment policy jointly with defense and selective-service officials, using public employment services, and enlisting management and labor. The child expands these elements into a comprehensive national manpower policy but preserves their distinctive combination and functional sequence. C03 supplies more specific occupational-deferment concepts, while C18 supplies the Office of Defense Mobilization’s coordination and directive machinery, but neither matches as much of the child’s substantive framework as C09.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Recruitment, placement, distribution, training, and utilization of the civilian labor force ... will be based primarily upon voluntary measures ... providing appropriate employment information ... developing recruitment ... training persons ... and providing appropriate placement services
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Secretary of Labor shall ... formulate plans, programs, and policies for meeting defense and essential civilian labor requirements [and] utilize the public employment service system, and enlist the cooperation and assistance of management and labor
shared_material.explanation: Both prescribe a coordinated civilian labor program centered on employment services, voluntary action, and cooperation with labor and management.

shared_material.child_excerpt: When the total need for workers with critical skills for civilian and military assignments is expected to exceed the supply ... distribution of the supply will be measured by the relative urgency of the need ... as between the Armed Forces and the civilian economy.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Assemble and analyze information on labor requirements for defense and other activities and on the supply of workers ... [and advise concerning] the relation of labor supply to materials and facilities requirements
shared_material.explanation: The child elaborates C09’s machinery for comparing labor requirements and supply and integrating manpower allocation with the broader defense-production program.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Policies governing occupational deferment ... [and] recruitment ... and call-up ... will have as their objective the use of persons possessing irreplaceable skills where they can make their maximum contribution
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Determine the occupations critical to meeting the labor requirements of defense and essential civilian activities and with the Secretary of Defense, the Director of Selective Service ... develop policies applicable to the induction and deferment of personnel for the armed services
shared_material.explanation: This is a close substantive and administrative parallel: identify critical occupations, balance defense and essential civilian needs, and coordinate induction and deferment policy with defense and selective-service authorities.
